source.title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: In the classical three-dimensional Skyrme model, finite-energy static fields define maps from R^3 ∪ {∞} ≅ S^3 to S^3, so each field has an integer topological degree N in π3(S^3). For every integer degree N, does there exist a finite-energy static field that minimizes the Skyrme energy among all configurations with degree N?

evidence.quote: In the classical Skyrme model, the field configurations are topologically represented by the homotopy group π3(S3) and the fundamental mathematical question is to ask whether there is a static Skyrme energy minimizer among each homotopy class.

accepted.question_text: In the Faddeev model, finite-energy static fields are maps n: R^3 → S^2 with Hopf invariant Q(n)=N, and the corresponding Faddeev knots are energy-minimizing configurations in a fixed Hopf class. For each nonzero integer N, does there exist a finite-energy static map with Hopf invariant N that minimizes the Faddeev energy among all maps with that Hopf invariant?

evidence.quote: solution configurations of the Hopf charge Q from Q = 1 up to Q = 8 and found that, for Q = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, the energy-minimizing solitons are ring-shaped and higher charges cause greater distortion, and for Q = 6, 7, 8, the solitons become knotted or linked. In particular, the trefoil knot appears at Q = 7. Thus, as in the case of the Skyrme model, we are facing again a topologically constrained minimization problem and our ultimate question is to find out whether there is a static Faddeev energy minimizer among each topological class defined by a nontrivial Hopf index (charge).

accepted.question_text: For the hyperbolic Euler-Lagrange equations governing the time-dependent Skyrme model and its Faddeev submodel in 3+1 dimensions, can one establish a mathematical well-posedness theory and determine the qualitative behavior of time-dependent solutions, including existence, uniqueness, regularity, and dynamical behavior for finite-energy data?

evidence.quote: we remark that there has been no mathematical study on the well-posedness of either the system of equations (3.16) and (3.17) or the equation (3.19), both hyperbolic, nor any study on the behavior of the time-dependent solutions of these important equations.

accepted.question_text: Let S be the set of integers N for which the Faddeev minimization problem EN = inf{E(n) | E(n) < ∞, Q(n) = N} is known to have a solution. The paper proves that S is infinite. Is S actually equal to all of Z, meaning that every integer Hopf charge is realized by an energy minimizer?

evidence.quote: Theorem 4.3. There exists an infinite subset S of the set Z of all integers so that for any N ∈ S the problem (3.24) has a solution. Although we do not know how big the set S is or whether S = Z, we can make the above statement more precise as follows.

accepted.question_text: Under the hedgehog ansatz in the three-dimensional Skyrme model, one obtains static critical points that minimize the energy within the radially symmetric class for each integer topological charge N. Are any of these hedgehog critical points absolute minimizers of the full Skyrme energy among all finite-energy fields of the same topological degree, rather than only within the radially symmetric subclass?

evidence.quote: that, for any integer N, (6.6) has a solution which may be obtained as the energy minimizer of (6.7) subject to the boundary condition stated in (6.6). See [26, 92]. In other words, among any topological class in π3(S3), the static Skyrme energy has a critical point which minimizes the energy functional among all radially symmetric field configurations. This result, although simple, is in sharp contrast with what we know for the sine–Gordon model where critical points of the energy of higher topological charges do not exist, as illustrated in Section 2. However, it is not known whether any of these critical points would be the absolute energy minimizers for the Skyrme model.

accepted.question_text: In the geometric Skyrme model for maps from the three-sphere S^3_R of radius R into the unit three-sphere S^3, there is a threshold R0 ∈ (√3/2, √2] such that for R < R0 the identity map x/R is the unique minimizer. Can this threshold be taken to be exactly √2?

evidence.quote: More recently, Riviere proved in [68] that, for the geometric Skyrme model governing maps from S3_R into S3, there is an R0 ∈ (√3/2, √2] such that for R < R0, the identity map x/R remains to be the unique minimizer. Whether or not one can take R0 to be equal to √2 remains open.

accepted.question_text: Let X = {n : R^3 → S^2, E(n) < ∞} be the finite-energy Sobolev class for the Faddeev model. Does every map n in X admit approximation by smooth maps n_j ∈ C∞(R^3, S^2) with uniformly bounded energy such that n_j → n in H^1_loc(R^3, S^2)?

evidence.quote: is well defined. Moreover, Q(n) ∈ Z as was shown in Theorem 3.3 of [50]. It is not clear, however, if any map n ∈ X can be approximated in L2_loc by a sequence of smooth maps nj ∈ C∞(R3, S2) such that E(nj) remains uniformly bounded. It is certainly unknown if n ∈ X can be approximated by a sequence of nj ∈ C∞(R3, S2) such that nj → n in H1_loc(R3, S2) and E(nj) remains to be uniformly bounded, as j → ∞. We refer to [37, 38, 39] for some recent works concerning such density questions of smooth maps in the spaces of Sobolev maps.

accepted.question_text: For the Faddeev minimization problem on bounded balls BR with constant boundary data and fixed Hopf charge N, let E^R_N be the minimum energy over maps BR → S^2 with Q(n)=N. As the radius R tends to infinity, does E^R_N converge to the full-space minimum EN? Equivalently, do minimizers on large bounded balls recover the full-space minimization problem in the limit?

evidence.quote: Energy splitting. For both Faddeev and Skyrme models, the existence of minimizers in every topological class of maps can be easily proved over a bounded contractible smooth domain in R3 (in particular, on a ball of radius R, say BR). Understanding of these minimizers as R → ∞ remains to be a difficult question. In fact, it is even unknown whether the minimum value (6.18) E^R_N = inf{E(n) | n : BR → S2, n|∂BR = const, Q(n) = N} satisfies E^R_N → EN as R → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Are absolute energy minimizers for the Skyrme and Faddeev models regular? More specifically, if one minimizes the corresponding constrained energy functional in a fixed topological class, must the resulting minimizer be smooth or otherwise enjoy strong regularity properties, rather than merely weak finite-energy regularity?

evidence.quote: Regularity. One of the most fundamental problems that remains open for both Skyrme and Faddeev models is the regularity of solutions. It may be relatively easier to check the regularity of those specially constructed solutions (such as the hedgehogs) as described above. It is however a difficult problem for the absolute energy minimizers. These questions are also closely related to similar questions in nonlinear elasticity.
